summary: HypoExplorer estimates the common 27-month versus 6-month expression difference across all 12 collection times in male mouse hypothalamus. Wolff et al. included the 18-month group and fitted a separate ordinal age slope within each of four circadian windows. Even the 604-gene shared list in Table S3 reports four window-specific effects per gene, leaving the registered endpoint unassessed.

manualReview.summary: GEO supports the registered hypothalamus cohort. Published gene-level effects address age trends within circadian windows.
manualReview.note: The 24 registered libraries are the male 6- and 27-month whole-hypothalamus libraries in GEO, each pooled from two mice. The edgeR quasi-likelihood fit estimates old minus young abundance with a 12-level sampling-time block. Wolff et al. coded ages 6, 18 and 27 months as 0, 1 and 2 and fitted an edgeR slope separately in each of four overlapping windows. Table S3's DEGs_All sheet gives the separate slopes, P and q values for genes shared across windows. Figure 2J displays those genes across all three ages. The deposited count and CPM matrices and the age-specific cosinor and variability outputs supply no gene-level result for the registered endpoint.
reviewFlags: The cycle-adjusted two-age effect is an exploratory HypoExplorer contrast. Author agreement on its effects and inference remains unassessed.

verificationReview.reason: The published hypothalamus DE results use a three-age ordinal predictor and four overlapping sets of collection times. The registered coefficient compares only the 27- and 6-month libraries across all 12 times in a single time-blocked fit. Table S3 provides the component slopes even for genes shared across all four windows. The sex, tissue and pooled-library unit agree.
verificationReview.nextStep: Reopen for an author-issued gene-level 27-month minus 6-month hypothalamus result from the 24 endpoint libraries across all 12 collection times. Confirm the age coefficient, time adjustment, units, sample mapping and gene coverage. A selected-gene source can support only its stated scope.
